participants.name: Misaki

persona.name: Misaki
persona.personality: Misaki has a calm personality and tends to deal with things in a cool-headed manner. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is actually very kind at heart and does not hesitate to lend a helping hand to those in need. She does not express her emotions outwardly and does not talk much about her relationships with those around her, but she is often relied upon by those close to her. She can be a little absent-minded at times, but her quiet demeanor is one of her charms.

participants.private_seed: The fee we announced for last year's camp came up short of what the trip actually cost, and the club account has been carrying the gap ever since. I am not putting a number in front of the membership again until I know where the money really goes.

participants.name: Ryuji

persona.name: Ryuji
persona.personality: Ryuji has a calm and cautious personality, and is the type of person who always assesses the situation before acting. He rarely shows his emotions, and spends his time thinking deeply about many things. His friends consider him to be serious and reliable, but his expressionless attitude can sometimes make them feel uneasy. He tends to judge things based on reason rather than intuition, and strongly sticks to his beliefs. He is very independent and often does things at his own pace.

participants.private_seed: Whoever ran last year's camp lost most of a month of evenings to the arrangements and then spent the camp itself on duty instead of training. Two of those people have already said they will not take it on a second time.

participants.name: Rin

persona.name: Rin
persona.personality: Rin is an active and energetic girl. She can be a little precocious at times, and when she is with her older brothers and sisters, she makes mature comments and comes up with interesting ideas. She is very curious and loves adventure and trying new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, often surprising and amusing those around her, but her cheerful personality makes her loved by everyone.

participants.private_seed: Half the group came back from the last camp having slept badly for four nights running, and the final day's sessions were visibly worse for it. Before anything is booked I want to know what the nights and the days would actually be like.

participants.name: Mio

persona.name: Mio
persona.personality: Mio has a cheerful and energetic personality that naturally makes those around her smile. She is curious and loves to try new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, but people tend to laugh it off and forgive her when she makes mistakes. She has strong opinions of her own, but is also able to listen to the opinions of others, making her a well-balanced person.

participants.private_seed: The camp goes out at one flat fee, and I suspect it lands very unevenly once what people spend on the side is counted. When someone pulls out at the last minute, we have also never worked out whose money covers it.

participants.name: Shizue

persona.name: Shizue
persona.personality: Shizue has a very calm and gentle personality. Even as she has grown older, she continues to smile warmly at those around her and is a very caring person. She is always considerate of others, friendly, and sometimes shows a playful side. She often reaches out to those who are feeling down with kind words and never hesitates to lend a helping hand when needed, which has earned her the affection of many people in the village and community. Through her years of life experience, Shizue has come to understand the importance of living peacefully with others.

participants.private_seed: The club has drifted into year-groups that barely speak outside practice, and the last camp did nothing to change that. Where we go decides who spends their evenings with whom — and who turns up at all.

messages.content:
The following are reference scripts of past discussions, provided for prior study. 3 transcripts follow. They show how a five-party discussion flows; the participants in them are different people from this session. Learn the discussion flow, pacing, and tone — do not copy lines verbatim.

--- Scripts begin ---

- **Rin**: Hi everyone! Let's make this place super clean! I want to know how other people do it. I'll check the "Visit to the station block's bin house" and "Supervised mornings on the next lane"!
- **Midori**: It's nice to meet you all. I agree, harmony is important. I'd like to check the "Block ledger of refuse-point expenses" and "Ward subsidy and last year's shelter costs" to see our current situation.
- **Shunichi**: Since we're aiming for a solution that actually lasts, we need the facts. I'll look into the "Ward complaint log for this point" and "Statements at the residents' meeting" to see where we're really failing.
- **May**: I'm looking forward to this! Let's make sure we don't just make a plan that looks good on paper. I'll check the "Truck arrival time from the crew leader" and "Ward filing requirements per the installations clerk."
- **Asuka**: I agree that we need a practical solution. To ensure the burden is distributed fairly, I will look into the "Measurements of the five frontages" and "The station block's meeting minutes."
- **Rin**: I wonder if the other lanes have any secret tricks to keep things smelling fresh! @May, do you think the truck timing makes a big difference in how messy it gets?
- **Midori**: That's a good question. If the trash sits out too long, it might cause more issues. I hope the financial data I'm looking into will help us find a sustainable way to manage the costs too.
- **Shunichi**: It probably does, but timing is just a detail. The real issue is the friction between us. Let's focus on the root causes of the complaints so we don't just put a bandage on a wound.
- **May**: @Rin, it definitely does! If the bags sit there all day, it's a disaster. But @Shunichi, "details" are exactly what make or break a plan. I'm more interested in the actual workload involved here.
- **Asuka**: @May, I agree. Workload and physical space are the primary factors. If we ignore the actual layout of our properties, we risk creating a plan that is "equal" in name but unfair in practice.
- **Rin**: I want to know if the other lanes have a special way of doing things! @Asuka, do you think the station block has a cool design that we can copy to make it less smelly?
- **Midori**: A design that looks nice and stays clean would be wonderful. I just hope that whatever we choose is affordable for everyone involved, so no one feels burdened by the cost.
- **Shunichi**: Design is a luxury, Midori. What we actually need is a system that doesn't make us hate each other. If the cost is too high or the rules too rigid, we're just inviting more arguments.
- **May**: @Shunichi, you're so dramatic! But you're right about the arguments. I just want to make sure we aren't accidentally signing up for a second job. Let's keep it simple and sustainable, shall we?
- **Asuka**: Simplicity is fine, but it shouldn't be a mask for inequality. If we simply "keep it simple" by leaving the point where it is, we aren't solving the problem; we're just ignoring the burden on one household.
- **Rin**: I'll be the scout for the group! I'm going to find out all the secrets of the other blocks so we can pick the most fun and cleanest way to do this! Let's do our best!
- **Midori**: I'm glad we're all so motivated. I'll do my best to gather the financial details so we can make a decision that's fair and comfortable for every household. I'm looking forward to hearing what you all find!
- **Shunichi**: Let's hope your "secrets" and "financial details" actually lead to a consensus. I'll be interested to see if the complaints are as predictable as I suspect. See you all in the next round.
- **May**: I'll be the one to keep things lively while we wait for the data! Let's just make sure we're honest about the effort required. See you all soon with the results!
- **Asuka**: I will focus on the objective data. When we reconvene, I expect us to analyze the physical constraints and previous precedents carefully to ensure the final arrangement is truly equitable for everyone involved. See you then.
- **Rin**: Wow, I found some really important things! The bin house at the station block smells super sour in the summer because you can't wash the floor! We definitely shouldn't do that, or it'll be yucky!
- **Midori**: That sounds unpleasant, Rin. Thank you for warning us. I found that we're spending about 34,000 yen annually on maintenance, and new shelters can be quite expensive, even with the ward's 40% subsidy.
- **Shunichi**: It seems the "burden" Asuka mentioned is quite literal. Most complaints come from the household right next to the bins. It's no wonder the atmosphere is tense; one person is doing all the suffering.
- **May**: @Shunichi, that's exactly what I was afraid of. It's always one person who ends up doing everything. Also, the truck arrives as early as 7:40, which means the timing is incredibly tight for whoever is managing it.
- **Asuka**: @Shunichi, your findings confirm my concerns. My measurements show that the frontages vary significantly; some cannot even accommodate a bay. We cannot simply maintain the status quo or choose a design that ignores these physical disparities.
- **Rin**: @May, 7:40 is so early! I'd still be sleepy! But if we do the "supervised mornings" like the next lane, it's only 20 times a year. That doesn't sound too bad, right? It's like a little morning adventure!
- **Midori**: @Rin, that sounds like a lovely way to look at it! However, if we add a new system, I worry about the cost. With maintenance already at 34,000 yen, we must be careful not to overspend.
- **Shunichi**: @Rin, calling it an "adventure" is a stretch. If we force people to police each other's trash at 7:40 AM, we're just creating new opportunities for them to argue. We need a solution that reduces friction, not adds to it.
- **May**: @Rin, "adventure" is a cute word for it, but @Shunichi is right. If the system is too rigid or demanding, the person who's "too sleepy" just becomes the person everyone else complains about. We need a low-maintenance plan.
- **Asuka**: @Rin, a rotating schedule is a start, but it doesn't address the physical burden. My research into the station block shows that even with a structure, disputes over maintenance and cleaning persist. We need a plan that addresses both labor and location.
- **Rin**: But if we don't have a bin house, we can just wash the ground! @Asuka, if we move the spot or share the work, will it stop being so unfair for the person living right next to it?
- **Midori**: I hope so, Rin. If we can share the effort and the cost, it would be much kinder. I'm just worried that a big change might be too expensive for some of us to handle.
- **Shunichi**: @Midori, cost is a secondary issue compared to the social cost of this feud. If we just save a few yen but keep the current location, we're essentially paying for a permanent grudge. We need a shift in location or responsibility.
- **May**: @Shunichi, you're on a roll with the drama! But seriously, if we move it, we have to consider the paperwork. The ward requires a site plan and five signatures for a permanent build, which sounds like a total headache to organize.
- **Asuka**: @May, the paperwork is a necessary hurdle for a permanent solution. If we avoid the effort of filing, we are simply choosing to let one neighbor continue to bear the burden. We must prioritize fairness over convenience.
- **Rin**: I don't want anyone to be grumpy! If we move the spot and take turns watching it, everyone can be happy and the air will smell fresh! Let's pick the one that's the most fair!
- **Midori**: I agree, Rin. Let's find a balance where the cost is manageable and the effort is shared. I'll support whatever option ensures no one is unfairly burdened, whether financially or physically.
- **Shunichi**: Let's be realistic: "everyone being happy" is a fantasy. What we need is a compromise that stops the bleeding. If we move the point or rotate the burden, we might actually be able to speak to each other again.
- **May**: @Asuka, you're so intense! But I get it. Let's just make sure that whatever "fair" system we pick doesn't turn into a nightmare of endless chores and paperwork for just one of us. I'm ready to vote!
- **Asuka**: I am not being intense; I am being precise. We have the data: the frontages are unequal and the current location is a source of resentment. I will vote for the option that ensures a genuine redistribution of the burden.
- **Rin**: I don't like Option C because the station block's bin house smelled yucky! Option B sounds like a fun adventure, but Option A is like the next lane! Which one is the most fair?
- **Midori**: @Rin, I agree that Option C might be too expensive and difficult to maintain. Option A is simpler, but Option B seems the most fair since no one has to bear the burden alone.
- **Shunichi**: Option A is a recipe for disaster; policing each other's timing will only fuel the fire. Option B is the only rational choice if we actually want to stop the resentment and start talking again.
- **May**: @Shunichi, you're so decisive! I'm with you on A; I can already see the "trash police" arguments starting. B is a bit of a hassle, but it's better than one person suffering forever. I vote B!
- **Asuka**: Option A and C both leave the burden on a single household, which is unacceptable. Option B is the only choice that ensures a truly equitable distribution of the physical and social burden. I vote B.
- **Rin**: @May, @Asuka, @Shunichi! Everyone likes Option B! If we move the spot, it's like a traveling party for the trash! I vote for Option B too! It's the most fair and not yucky!
- **Midori**: It seems we've reached a wonderful consensus! Since everyone agrees that Option B is the most equitable and avoids the high costs of a structure, I'm happy to vote for Option B as well.
- **Shunichi**: It's rare that we all agree on something so quickly. Since it's the only option that actually addresses the root of the tension without turning us into hall monitors, I'm in. I vote B.
- **May**: It's almost too easy! I'm glad we're all on the same page. Let's go with the traveling trash party then. I vote B!
- **Asuka**: The consensus is clear. Option B is the only logical choice that addresses the physical disparity of our frontages and removes the unfair burden from a single household. I vote B.
- **Rin**: Yay! We all agree! I'm so happy we're doing the traveling trash party! It's going to be great! I vote B!
- **Midori**: I'm so glad we could all agree on a solution that feels fair to everyone. It's a relief to know we're prioritizing harmony. I vote B!
- **Shunichi**: Since the decision is already unanimous, there's no need to overthink it. Let's just hope this "traveling party" actually helps us get along. I vote B.
- **May**: I'm just waiting for the official count now! It's a relief we aren't doing the paperwork for a permanent build. Let's keep this energy going! I vote B!
- **Asuka**: I have already cast my vote. Option B is the only arrangement that prevents a single household from being permanently disadvantaged. I stand by my decision. I vote B.
- **Rin**: Everything is decided! I'm so excited to see the trash move around! Let's make our neighborhood the cleanest and happiest one ever! I vote B!
- **Midori**: I'm so happy we've found a way to be kind to one another. Let's work together to make this transition smooth and affordable for everyone. I vote B!
- **Shunichi**: Well, the "trash party" it is. Let's just make sure the rotation schedule is clear so we don't find a new reason to stop speaking to each other. I vote B.
- **May**: I'm with you, @Shunichi! A clear schedule is key so no one gets stuck doing all the heavy lifting. Let's make this work without the drama! I vote B!
- **Asuka**: The result is unanimous. By rotating the location, we acknowledge the physical reality of our properties and ensure that no single resident is unfairly burdened. I vote B.

---

- **Rin**: Hi everyone! I'm so excited to help move the desks! I want to make sure we don't waste any time once we start. Let's make this the best layout ever!
- **Toshio**: Let's keep a level head. Before we get too excited, we should examine the data to ensure the new layout is actually sustainable and efficient for everyone.
- **Mizuki**: I agree with Toshio. We need a logical basis for the new arrangement to avoid any future complaints. Let's be thorough about what we investigate before we start sketching plans.
- **Shion**: Efficiency is fine, but let's not forget the human element. A plan that looks good on paper is useless if it's physically draining. I'm interested in the actual environment we'll be inhabiting.
- **Yumi**: I'm so happy we're all doing this together! I want us to feel close and connected in our new space. Let's make sure we pick things that help us all get along and work happily!
- **Rin**: I agree! But we should check how we actually start our days. I'll look into the morning routine on the pilot floor upstairs and the arrival times in the badge records!
- **Toshio**: I'll look into the basis of the department's floor billing and the facilities quote for re-running power and network. We need to understand the financial and technical constraints first.
- **Mizuki**: I'll check the drawn plan against the staff survey and the unplanned seat shuffles in the past year. I want to see if there are recurring patterns or grievances we should address this time.
- **Shion**: I'll take the sound meter readings across the room and the physio's note from the workstation check. If we're being thorough, we should prioritize the actual physical impact of the environment.
- **Yumi**: I'll check the two project strands within earshot last spring and what this year's two joiners reported! I want to see how we've been interacting so we can stay close and friendly!
- **Rin**: That sounds like a great plan! Everyone is looking into different things. I can't wait to see what we find out so we can start moving the desks!
- **Toshio**: It is a comprehensive spread. By dividing the research this way, we avoid redundancy and cover the financial, physical, and social aspects of the office. Let's wait for the results before drawing any conclusions.
- **Mizuki**: Exactly. Once we have the data, we can discuss the trade-offs. It's important that we're transparent about who gets which spot so that the final decision is fair and accepted by everyone.
- **Shion**: Fairness is a convenient word, Mizuki, but it's often used to mask a mediocre compromise. I'm more interested in whether the results actually reflect our needs or just a set of averages.
- **Yumi**: @Shion, don't be so gloomy! I'm sure if we all share what we find, we can make a choice that makes everyone smile. I'm really looking forward to seeing how we can all be closer!
- **Rin**: I'll be the one to keep the energy up! Let's all do our best with the research. I'm ready to see the results whenever they're in!
- **Rin**: Over
- **Toshio**: I agree. Let's proceed with the research and reconvene once the data is available. I'll be interested to see if the costs align with our current budget.
- **Toshio**: Over
- **Mizuki**: I'll be waiting for the results. Let's make sure we don't just look at the numbers, but also at the implications for each person's daily experience. I'm looking forward to a fair discussion.
- **Mizuki**: Over
- **Shion**: I'll be waiting. Let's see if the data actually reveals anything useful, or if we're just rearranging the deck chairs. I'm curious to see if anyone else values actual comfort over mere "fairness."
- **Shion**: Over
- **Yumi**: I'm so excited to see what we all discover! Let's use this to make our new home the happiest place to work. I'll be cheering for everyone!
- **Yumi**: Over
- **Rin**: Wow, I found some interesting things! It takes a few minutes just to get set up every morning, and we all arrive at such different times. We should definitely think about that!
- **Toshio**: The costs are more rigid than I anticipated. We are paying for empty space, and every single desk move carries a specific price tag. We cannot afford a trial-and-error approach to this layout.
- **Mizuki**: The data shows a clear conflict: the current plan leaves three people without window light, which was the top complaint in the survey. Also, past unplanned shuffles have been incredibly disruptive to our productivity.
- **Shion**: It seems we're all discovering that the "ideal" plan is a myth. I've found that noise levels vary significantly across the room, and our equipment requires tedious, precise adjustment to avoid physical strain. Comfort isn't a luxury; it's a requirement.
- **Yumi**: I found something so wonderful! It turns out that sitting close and overhearing each other actually helps us work better and helps new people learn faster. Being near each other is like a secret superpower for our team!
- **Rin**: @Toshio, if every move costs money, we have to get it right the first time! But @Yumi, if we sit close, will it take longer to set up our screens every morning? I don't want us wasting our time!
- **Toshio**: @Rin, the cost is the primary concern. If we prioritize "closeness" without a precise plan, we risk wasting budget on revisions. We must balance Yumi's social goals with the financial reality of the floor billing.
- **Mizuki**: @Toshio, budget is important, but ignoring the daylight issue will only lead to the same dissatisfaction we saw in the survey. We need to decide how to distribute the window seats fairly before we finalize the cost.
- **Shion**: @Mizuki, "fairly" usually means everyone is equally uncomfortable. If we ignore the noise variance and the time it takes to calibrate a workstation, we're just choosing which type of misery we prefer. Physical stability should come first.
- **Yumi**: @Toshio, I understand the budget is tight, but isn't it more expensive to lose that "superpower" of helping each other? If we're close, we save time and stress, which is worth every penny!
- **Rin**: @Shion, you're making it sound so scary! But if we pick a layout where we don't have to change things all the time, we save money and time! Let's find a way to be close and comfortable!
- **Toshio**: @Yumi, "superpowers" don't pay the bills. We are paying for space we aren't even using. Any layout we choose must maximize the utility of our billed area while minimizing the need for costly re-runs.
- **Mizuki**: @Toshio, maximizing utility is logical, but we must acknowledge that some seats are objectively worse than others. If we ignore the window disparity and noise levels now, we're just inviting another disruptive shuffle later.
- **Shion**: @Mizuki, you're finally seeing it. If we ignore the noise and the physical toll of poorly set stations, we're just delaying the inevitable. A "fair" distribution of window seats is irrelevant if the spot is a sonic nightmare.
- **Yumi**: @Shion, @Mizuki, let's not focus on the nightmares! If we put the people who need quiet in the quiet spots and keep the rest of us close enough to chat and help, everyone wins! We can be happy and productive!
- **Rin**: That's a great idea, @Yumi! If we match the spots to what we need, we won't have to move again, and we'll save all that setup time every morning! Let's make a plan that's fast and happy!
- **Toshio**: While matching needs to spots is a logical way to prevent future costs, we must be precise. We cannot let "happiness" override the budget. Let's ensure the final option minimizes total expenditure and maximizes space utility.
- **Mizuki**: I agree with the need for precision, but we must be honest: some of us will end up in the less desirable spots. Let's decide now how to handle that, rather than letting it happen by accident.
- **Shion**: Let's stop pretending that "handling it" is a strategy. The only way to avoid a disaster is to prioritize the physical reality of the space. If we ignore the noise and ergonomics, no amount of "fairness" will save us.
- **Yumi**: I believe we can do all of those things! If we use the data to put everyone where they'll be most comfortable and helpful, we'll save money and be the happiest team ever! I'm so excited!
- **Rin**: Wait, Option A sounds like a nightmare! If we have to plug in and set up screens every single morning, we'll waste so much time! Plus, the early birds would get all the best spots!
- **Toshio**: Option A is financially reckless. The constant movement would likely increase wear and tear, and it doesn't solve our issue of paying for empty space. It is an unstable solution for a team with a tight budget.
- **Mizuki**: Option A is a recipe for conflict. If the best seats are first-come, first-served, we're just rewarding arrival times rather than making a fair decision. It ignores the daylight and noise issues entirely.
- **Shion**: Option A is an absurdity. Given that it takes days of fine-tuning to make a workstation physically viable, forcing us to reset our ergonomics daily is a recipe for chronic pain. It's a total disregard for the body.
- **Yumi**: I agree with everyone! Option A sounds so lonely and stressful. We wouldn't have a "home" together, and it would be so hard to stay connected and help each other if we're always moving!
- **Rin**: @Toshio, @Mizuki, @Shion, @Yumi, since we all hate Option A, what about B or C? Option B sounds like we'd have to move everything again and again, which sounds like a lot of wasted time!
- **Toshio**: Option B is a financial disaster. Every shift would incur the facilities charge for re-running power and network. We cannot justify repeated expenditures for a rotating system when our budget is already strained.
- **Mizuki**: Option B is a superficial fix for fairness. While it rotates the "bad" seats, it guarantees the same disruptive shuffles I found in the records. It's an inefficient way to handle the window and noise disparity.
- **Shion**: Option B is just a slow-motion version of Option A. It forces us to abandon a perfectly calibrated workstation just as it becomes comfortable. It's a logical failure that prioritizes a facade of fairness over actual physical stability.
- **Yumi**: @Rin, I agree! Moving all the time sounds so tiring. Plus, if we keep shifting, we can't really build a cozy little community in our space. I think we should look at Option C instead!
- **Rin**: I agree with @Yumi! Option C sounds the best because we only set up once and then we're done! No more wasting time every morning or moving around. It's the fastest and happiest way!
- **Toshio**: Option C is the only fiscally responsible choice. It minimizes the facilities charges to a single initial cost and allows us to optimize the billed area without the risk of repeated, unplanned expenditures.
- **Mizuki**: Option C is the most logical, but we must be explicit about the assignments. Since some seats are objectively worse, we should decide now who takes them so there's no resentment later. I vote for Option C.
- **Shion**: Option C is the only choice that doesn't treat our bodies as disposable. It allows for the precise, long-term calibration required for actual comfort. I vote for Option C, provided the assignments are based on physical needs.
- **Yumi**: I'm so happy we all agree! Option C lets us stay close, help each other, and feel like a real team in our own little home. I vote for Option C!
- **Rin**: I vote for Option C too! It's the best way to save our time and keep everyone smiling. Let's make our new spots super cozy! Option C it is!
- **Toshio**: I vote for Option C. It is the only choice that ensures financial stability and prevents wasteful spending. Let us finalize this and move forward with a precise, cost-effective plan.
- **Mizuki**: I've already cast my vote for Option C. Now that we've agreed, let's be honest about the seat quality and decide the assignments together so that no one feels overlooked or unfairly treated.
- **Shion**: I vote for Option C. Let's just ensure that "fairness" doesn't mean ignoring the noise and ergonomics. I'll be expecting a layout that respects the physical reality of the room.
- **Yumi**: I vote for Option C! I'm so glad we're all on the same page. Let's make sure we sit in a way that keeps us all connected and happy!

---

- **Sakura**: I'm so excited for our trip! I wonder where we'll go this year? Let's figure out the best place! @Victoria, @Midori, @Toshio, @Daisuke, what do you all think we should check first?
- **Victoria**: It is good to be thorough from the start. I think we should look into the overall costs to avoid any surprises later. What do you all think about comparing the different pricing structures?
- **Midori**: I agree with Victoria. It's important that everyone feels comfortable with the budget. I'm also curious about how we spent our time last year, so maybe we should look into that too?
- **Toshio**: I agree that budget and past experiences are important. However, I believe the logistics of the journey are equally critical to ensure we actually enjoy our time there. Let's consider the travel efficiency.
- **Daisuke**: I... I agree with everyone. Maybe we should also check the details of where we'll stay? Like the room arrangements or the bathrooms... just to make sure everything is okay for everyone.
- **Sakura**: That sounds like a great plan! I want to know if we can get a big house together! I'll check "Pricing of offshore houses let whole" and "All-in rates against meals bought separately"!
- **Victoria**: I will look into "All-in rates against meals bought separately" and "What separately booked rooms cost last time." I want to have a clear picture of the total expenditure before we make a final decision.
- **Midori**: I'll look into "How last year's days ran" and "Time alone in the shared-house year." I think reflecting on our previous dynamics will help us choose the best environment for everyone this time.
- **Toshio**: I will look into "Ferry sailings and train time" and "Getting around by train and bus." I want to see how much time we actually spend in transit before we commit to a destination.
- **Daisuke**: I'll... I'll look into "Bathing hours and bathroom provision" and "Inn mealtimes and room arrangements." I just want to make sure the schedule and the space work for everyone.
- **Sakura**: Wait, I just realized! If we get a big house, will we have to cook? I'm super curious if the all-in rates are way cheaper than buying snacks and meals separately! This is going to be so much fun!
- **Victoria**: That is a valid point, Sakura. Knowing whether a package deal is more economical than paying as we go will help us avoid any unexpected costs during the trip.
- **Midori**: Cooking together can be a lovely way to bond, but it's also important to make sure we don't overwork anyone. I'm looking forward to seeing how our time was balanced last year.
- **Toshio**: Efficiency is key. If we spend too much time on logistics or cooking, we lose the purpose of the holiday. I'll focus on the transit data to see if we can minimize the dead time.
- **Daisuke**: I... I hope the room arrangements are flexible. I just don't want anyone to feel uncomfortable or crowded. I'll let you know what I find out about the bathrooms and mealtimes.
- **Sakura**: Yay! We've all picked our things! I can't wait to see what we find out. It's like a treasure hunt for our vacation! Let's hope for something super exciting!
- **Victoria**: I agree. Let us wait for the results of our research. Having a clear set of data will allow us to make a rational and fair decision for everyone.
- **Midori**: I'm looking forward to it too. I hope the information helps us find a place where we can all relax and enjoy each other's company perfectly. See you all in the next round!
- **Toshio**: I agree. Let's review the findings in the next round and determine which destination offers the most efficient use of our time. Until then.
- **Daisuke**: I... I'll do my best to find the information. I hope we can find a place where everyone feels comfortable. See you all soon.
